title: "rush run"

```{term}
#| include: false
rush run -o mtcars.csv 'mtcars'
```

The `run` command evaluates an R expression and prints or saves its value. If
you give it files, they are read into data frames first. It is the core
command of `rush`.

## Usage

```bash
rush run [options] [<expression>] [--] [<file>...]
```

## Expressions

`rush run` evaluates any R expression and prints its value:

```{term}
rush run '6 * 7'
```

Separate multiple expressions with semicolons (or newlines). The value of the
last one is printed:

```{term}
rush run 'x <- 1:10; mean(x)'
```

Vectors are printed one element per line, so they work well with other
command-line tools:

```{term}
rush run 'rev(LETTERS[1:5])'
```

## Input

### Files

Pass one or more files after the expression. The first is read into a data
frame called `df`:

```{term}
rush run 'nrow(df)' mtcars.csv
```

The reader is chosen by the file extension. See [Formats](../formats.qmd) for
all of them, and `--input-format` (`-F`) to override the choice.

### The `df` and `dfs` variables

Two variables are always available in your expression:

- **`df`**: the first input. For a database file (DuckDB or SQLite), this is a
  named list of its tables.
- **`dfs`**: a named list of all inputs, named after the file names without
  their extension. Database tables are nested one level deeper:
  `dfs$dbname$tablename`.

```{term}
rush run -o fast.csv 'dplyr::filter(df, hp > 200)' mtcars.csv
rush run 'names(dfs)' mtcars.csv fast.csv
rush run 'nrow(dfs$fast)' mtcars.csv fast.csv
```

### Standard input

Use `-` as the file name to read from standard input:

```{term}
printf 'name,score\nAlice,92\nBob,85\nCarol,97\n' |
  rush run 'dplyr::arrange(df, dplyr::desc(score))' -
```

Without `-`, `rush run` doesn't read standard input, so an expression that
uses `df` or `dfs` is an error. Standard input is read as CSV; use `-F` for
another format:

```{term}
rush run -O json 'head(df, 2)' mtcars.csv |
  rush run -F json 'dplyr::select(df, mpg, hp)' -
```

## Output

Where the result goes depends on `--output` (`-o`), `--output-format` (`-O`),
and whether standard output is a terminal:

| The result is | In a terminal | Piped or redirected |
|---------------|---------------|---------------------|
| A data frame  | A table       | CSV                 |
| A vector      | One element per line | The same     |
| A named vector or a matrix | A table | CSV            |
| A ggplot      | ANSI art      | PNG                 |
| Anything else | As R prints it | The same           |

### Terminal and pipe

In a terminal, a data frame is printed as a table:

```{term}
rush run 'head(df, 3)' mtcars.csv
```

Piped into another command, it is written as CSV, which `cat` shows here:

```{term}
rush run 'head(df, 3)' mtcars.csv | cat
```

A named vector, such as a count with `table()`, and a matrix, such as a
correlation matrix, keep their names:

```{term}
rush run 'table(df$cyl)' mtcars.csv
rush run 'round(cor(df[c("mpg", "hp", "wt")]), 2)' mtcars.csv
```

Anything else, such as a model, is printed as R prints it:

```{term}
rush run 'lm(mpg ~ wt, df)' mtcars.csv
```

A ggplot is drawn as a plot. See [`rush plot`](plot.qmd#output) for its output
formats:

```{term}
rush run -l ggplot2 'ggplot(df, aes(wt, mpg)) + geom_point()' mtcars.csv
```

### `--output` (`-o`)

Write the result to a file. The format is inferred from the extension:

```{term}
rush run -o fast.parquet 'dplyr::filter(df, hp > 200)' mtcars.csv
rush run 'dim(df)' fast.parquet
```

### `--output-format` (`-O`)

Write another format to standard output. An explicit `-O` is used in the
terminal too:

```{term}
rush run -O json 'head(df[1:3], 2)' mtcars.csv
```

### `--head`

Write only the first rows of a data frame:

```{term}
rush run --head 2 'df' mtcars.csv | cat
```

### `--width` (`-w`), `--height`

Limit the width and the number of rows of a table in the terminal. (For plots,
they set the size of the plot.)

```{term}
rush run -w 50 --height 3 'df' mtcars.csv
```

### Format-specific options

- `--output-delimiter` (`-D`): the delimiter of
  [delimited text](../formats/delimited.qmd#output-delimiter--d)
- `--output-sheet`: the sheet name of an
  [Excel or ODS file](../formats/excel.qmd#output-sheet)
- `--output-indent`: the indentation of JSON and YAML (2 by default)
- `--output-root`, `--output-record`: the element names of
  [XML](../formats/structured.qmd#xml), and the table name of TOML

```{term}
rush run -O xml --output-root garage --output-record car 'head(df[1:3], 2)' \
  mtcars.csv
```

## Reading options

These options control how files are read. The page on
[delimited text](../formats/delimited.qmd) shows them in more detail.

- `--delimiter` (`-d`): the delimiter for reading and writing (`,` by
  default)
- `--input-delimiter`: the delimiter for reading only
- `--input-format` (`-F`): the format of the input, instead of the extension
- `--input-sheet`: the sheet of an [Excel or ODS file](../formats/excel.qmd)
- `--no-header` (`-H`), `--no-input-header`, `--no-output-header`: files
  without a header row
- `--names`: column names for a file without a header row
- `--no-clean-names` (`-C`): keep the column names as they are

For example, `-H` reads columns without a header as `x1`, `x2`, and so on:

```{term}
seq 5 | rush run -H 'cumsum(df$x1)' -
```

## Setup options

### `--tidyverse` (`-t`)

Load the [tidyverse](https://www.tidyverse.org/) (and glue), so you can use
dplyr, tidyr, stringr, and friends without the `package::` prefix:

```{term}
rush run -t 'df |> group_by(cyl) |> summarise(avg_mpg = mean(mpg))' mtcars.csv
```

### `--library` (`-l`)

Load packages, separated by commas. `rush` installs them when needed. You
don't need `-l` for a package you only call with `pkg::`, such as
`readxl::excel_sheets()`: `rush` installs those too.

```{term}
rush run -l dplyr,tidyr 'df |>
  pivot_longer(c(mpg, hp), names_to = "metric") |>
  count(metric)' mtcars.csv
```

### `--seed`

Set the seed of the random number generator, for reproducible results:

```{term}
rush run --seed 42 'sample(1:100, 5)'
```

## General options

### `--dry-run` (`-n`)

Print the generated R script instead of running it. See
[Scripts](../scripts.qmd) for how to save and run it:

```{term}
rush run -n 'dplyr::filter(df, mpg > 25)' mtcars.csv
```

### `--no-rush` (`-R`)

Combined with `--dry-run`, print a script that doesn't need `rush` to run:
every helper is inlined. See [Scripts](../scripts.qmd#scripts-without-rush).

### `--no-ir` (`-I`)

Run the script with `Rscript` instead of `ir`, using the packages installed in
your R library. See [Scripts](../scripts.qmd#running-without-ir).

### `--verbose` (`-v`)

Print the parsed options to standard error before running. Useful when an
option doesn't do what you expect:

```{term}
rush run -v --seed 7 'sum(1:10)'
```

### `--version`

```{term}
rush --version
```

## Help

```{term}
rush run -h
```

```{term}
#| include: false
rm -f mtcars.csv fast.csv fast.parquet
```
